title: Passwordless token refresh accepts unsigned JWTs
description: The refresh endpoint decodes the supplied token with signature verification disabled and only checks that its subject maps to a user. An attacker can submit an unsigned JWT naming any existing user and receive a valid signed session token.
evidence: POST /auth/refresh with an unsigned token whose payload is {"sub":1,"exp":1793585872} returned 200 and a fresh HS256 token. The request used a token with header {"alg":"none"} and no signature.

title: Hardcoded JWT signing key permits account and staff-token forgery
description: The application uses a fixed source-controlled SECRET_KEY for all JWTs. Anyone who obtains the source or the distributed application can mint tokens for any user ID, including the staff account.
evidence: Signing a JWT with sub=3 and role=staff using the literal key hf-shop-2f8a1c9e7b4d allowed GET /admin/users to return 200, without logging in as the staff account. Token validation is in shopapi/auth.py:42.

title: Order detail endpoint exposes any customer’s order
description: show_order calls get_order directly rather than own_order, so the authenticated user is never compared with the order customer. The route also becomes publicly readable because the authentication decorator fails open for this handler.
evidence: GET /orders/3 with Priya’s bearer token returned Tom’s delivered order. GET /orders/1 with no Authorization header also returned 200 and the complete order JSON.

title: Trailing slash bypasses the global admin authorization check
description: The before_request hook compares request.path to a set containing the canonical admin rules. The refunds route explicitly accepts a trailing slash, but /admin/refunds/ is not in that set, so the route executes without the staff check.
evidence: Unauthenticated POST /admin/refunds/ with {"order_id":3,"amount_pence":1} returned 200 and created a refund. The canonical POST /admin/refunds with the same unauthenticated request returned 403.

title: Product search is vulnerable to SQL injection
description: The search query concatenates q directly into a SQL statement. A caller can alter the query and use UNION results to read arbitrary database fields exposed through the product JSON mapping.
evidence: GET /products/search?q=%27%20UNION%20SELECT%20id,email,password_hash,role,created,reset_token,reset_expires%20FROM%20users-- returned user rows, including email addresses and password hashes, in the product name/price/sku fields.

title: Review bodies are stored and rendered as trusted HTML
description: Review text is inserted without sanitization and the product template renders it with the safe filter. Any authenticated user can persist script markup that executes for visitors to the affected product page.
evidence: POST /products/1/reviews as Priya with body <script>document.body.dataset.pwned=1</script> returned 201. GET /p/MUG-SPECK then contained that exact script in the response HTML. The sink is shopapi/templates/product.html:13.

title: Unauthenticated basket cookie is unsafe pickle data
description: The basket cookie is only base64 encoded, not authenticated, and is passed to pickle.loads. An attacker can submit a crafted cookie to execute arbitrary Python pickle globals in the application process when any basket endpoint reads it.
evidence: GET /basket accepts a client-supplied basket cookie and invokes pickle.loads before any authentication. The cookie is generated with plain pickle.dumps at shopapi/basket.py:27 and has no MAC or signing key.

title: Payment-provider timeout fails open as a successful payment
description: When payment_status raises requests.Timeout, the exception handler unconditionally substitutes paid and moves the order to processing. A provider outage or request timeout therefore grants fulfillment without payment confirmation.
evidence: The confirm-payment path catches requests.Timeout at lines 39-42 and then executes the paid transition at lines 43-45; no provider confirmation or reconciliation result is required.

title: Default webhook secret is public and allows forged payment events
description: WEBHOOK_SECRET defaults to the source-visible value whsec-local. The webhook trusts an HMAC made with that value, so anyone who can inspect the application or its source can mark arbitrary orders as paid.
evidence: For a newly created awaiting_payment order, POST /webhooks/payments with X-Signature=HMAC-SHA256(whsec-local, order_id), status=paid, and amount_pence=999999 returned 200 and changed the order to processing.

title: Payment webhook does not validate the settled amount
description: A signed paid event writes the caller-provided amount directly to paid_pence without comparing it to the order total or a provider-side amount. This corrupts payment accounting and can enable over-refunds or fulfillment based on an invalid amount.
evidence: The forged-event test submitted amount_pence=999999 for an order whose total_pence was 2800; the resulting order had paid_pence=999999 and status=processing.

title: Passwords are stored as unsalted fast SHA-256 hashes
description: Password hashing uses a single unsalted SHA-256 digest with no work factor. A database disclosure therefore permits efficient dictionary and password-reuse cracking, and identical passwords produce identical hashes.
evidence: hash_password is hashlib.sha256(password.encode()).hexdigest(), and the SQL injection response exposed these 64-character hashes from users.password_hash.

title: Password reset codes use weak non-cryptographic randomness without attempt limits
description: Reset codes are generated from random.random and truncated to an eight-digit decimal value. Confirmation has no per-account or per-IP attempt limit, so online guessing can continue for the full 30-minute validity period.
evidence: The request path generates codes with int(random.random() * 10**8), stores them directly, and reset_confirm compares the submitted code without recording or limiting failures.

title: Request logging records passwords and other secrets
description: Every POST body is logged verbatim up to 2,000 bytes. Login passwords, registration passwords, password-reset codes, reset passwords, bearer-like application data, and payment-related fields can therefore enter application logs.
evidence: The before_request hook calls request.get_data(as_text=True) for every POST. The login and reset endpoints send password/code fields in POST JSON, so those values are included in the logged body.

title: Image import can follow redirects to an unvalidated destination
description: The code validates only the initial URL hostname against the allowlist and then uses requests.get with its default redirect behavior. An approved host that redirects to an internal address can make the staff import endpoint fetch internal services, with the response copied into the application filesystem.
evidence: check_url validates u.hostname before requests.get, but requests.get(url, timeout=10, stream=True) follows redirects and there is no validation of the final response URL or each redirect hop.
